title: Fix it: rename every key, everywhere, at any depth
prompt:
The script in the editor is **almost** right. It passes on the sample and fails on a case you cannot see.

The original task was:

You are given JSON of unknown shape — objects nested inside arrays nested inside objects, to any depth. Every key that uses `snake_case` has to come out `camelCase`, no matter how deep it sits.

Only keys change. A value is left exactly as it is, even if it happens to be a string that itself looks like `snake_case` — `"account_status": "in_progress"` becomes `"accountStatus": "in_progress"`, not `"accountStatus": "inProgress"`.

The input is not always an object at the top. It can be an array, and arrays can hold plain scalars as well as objects — a list of tags, for instance, sitting next to a list of line items.

Find what is wrong and fix it. You can press Run to see what it currently does.
starter:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun camelKey(s) = do {
  var parts = s splitBy "_"
  var rest = parts[1 to -1] default []
  ---
  parts[0] ++ ((rest map ((w) -> upper(w[0] default "") ++ (w[1 to -1] default ""))) joinBy "")
}
fun rewrite(v) = v match {
  case o is Object -> o mapObject ((val, key) -> { (camelKey(key)): rewrite(val) })
  case a is Array -> a map ((elem) -> elem mapObject ((val, key) -> { (camelKey(key)): rewrite(val) }))
  else -> v
}
---
rewrite(payload)
hints: Run it on the sample first. If the sample looks right, the bug only shows on data the sample does not contain.
Ask what kind of input would break this — an empty list, a missing field, a value ordered differently.
the Array branch assumes every element is an Object and calls mapObject on it directly, so it works on nested objects but throws the moment it meets an array of plain scalars, such as special_tags
solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun camelKey(s) = do {
  var parts = s splitBy "_"
  var rest = parts[1 to -1] default []
  ---
  parts[0] ++ ((rest map ((w) -> upper(w[0] default "") ++ (w[1 to -1] default ""))) joinBy "")
}
fun rewrite(v) = v match {
  case o is Object -> o mapObject ((val, key) -> { (camelKey(key)): rewrite(val) })
  case a is Array -> a map rewrite($)
  else -> v
}
---
rewrite(payload)

mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun camelKey(s) = do {
  var parts = s splitBy "_"
  var rest = parts[1 to -1] default []
  ---
  parts[0] ++ ((rest map ((w) -> upper(w[0] default "") ++ (w[1 to -1] default ""))) joinBy "")
}
fun rewrite(v) = v match {
  case o is Object -> o mapObject ((val, key) -> { (camelKey(key)): rewrite(val) })
  case a is Array -> a map ((elem) -> elem mapObject ((val, key) -> { (camelKey(key)): rewrite(val) }))
  else -> v
}
---
rewrite(payload)

explanation.approach: There is no built-in that walks arbitrary JSON and renames keys — the shape isn't known until you're looking at the value in front of you, so the walk has to be written as a recursive function with one branch per kind of value: an Object renames its own keys with `mapObject` and recurses into each value; an Array just recurses into each element, unchanged in kind; anything else (`String`, `Number`, `Boolean`, `null`) is a leaf and comes back untouched. `dw::util::Tree`'s `mapLeafValues` looks like it should help — it also walks a whole structure — but it transforms leaf VALUES, and this task is about KEYS, so it doesn't apply here. The part that actually catches people is the Array branch: it's tempting to assume every array holds more objects, but an array can just as easily hold scalars, and calling an object-only function on a scalar element is a hard error, not a smaller correct answer.

snippets.label: camelKey on its own, including a mid-word digit
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun camelKey(s) = do {
  var parts = s splitBy "_"
  var rest = parts[1 to -1] default []
  ---
  parts[0] ++ ((rest map ((w) -> upper(w[0] default "") ++ (w[1 to -1] default ""))) joinBy "")
}
---
{
  a: camelKey("user_id"),
  b: camelKey("full_name"),
  c: camelKey("item_2_id"),
  d: camelKey("already")
}
snippets.note: Splitting on `_` and capitalizing the first letter of every part after the first — a key with no underscore at all just comes back unchanged, which is what `camelKey("already")` shows.

snippets.label: The full recursive walk on the sample
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun camelKey(s) = do {
  var parts = s splitBy "_"
  var rest = parts[1 to -1] default []
  ---
  parts[0] ++ ((rest map ((w) -> upper(w[0] default "") ++ (w[1 to -1] default ""))) joinBy "")
}
fun rewrite(v) = v match {
  case o is Object -> o mapObject ((val, key) -> { (camelKey(key)): rewrite(val) })
  case a is Array -> a map rewrite($)
  else -> v
}
---
rewrite(payload)
snippets.note: Object keys are renamed at every level; the array of phone numbers passes through the Array branch and each String inside hits `else`, so the numbers themselves are untouched.

snippets.label: mapLeafValues walks the whole tree too, but it never sees the keys
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
import * from dw::util::Tree
output application/json
---
mapLeafValues({user_id: 1, full_name: "Ada"}, (v, p) -> v)
snippets.note: Even though the callback runs on every leaf, the keys `user_id` and `full_name` come back exactly as they went in — `mapLeafValues` is a value-mapper, not a key-mapper, so it cannot do this task no matter what the callback does.

snippets.label: Why the Array branch can't assume every element is an Object
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun camelKey(s) = do {
  var parts = s splitBy "_"
  var rest = parts[1 to -1] default []
  ---
  parts[0] ++ ((rest map ((w) -> upper(w[0] default "") ++ (w[1 to -1] default ""))) joinBy "")
}
fun rewrite(v) = v match {
  case o is Object -> o mapObject ((val, key) -> { (camelKey(key)): rewrite(val) })
  case a is Array -> a map ((elem) -> elem mapObject ((val, key) -> { (camelKey(key)): rewrite(val) }))
  else -> v
}
---
rewrite(payload)
snippets.note: This version renames nested objects fine right up until the Array branch reaches `phone_numbers`, whose elements are Strings. Calling `mapObject` on a String is `UnexpectedFunctionCallTypesException`, not a partial result — the whole script fails on a payload that looks perfectly ordinary.

snippets.label: A scalar at the top has no keys to rename
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun camelKey(s) = do {
  var parts = s splitBy "_"
  var rest = parts[1 to -1] default []
  ---
  parts[0] ++ ((rest map ((w) -> upper(w[0] default "") ++ (w[1 to -1] default ""))) joinBy "")

fun rewrite(v) = v match {
  case o is Object -> o mapObject ((val, key) -> { (camelKey(key)): rewrite(val) })
  case a is Array -> a map rewrite($)
  else -> v
}
---
rewrite(payload)
snippets.note: A bare String hits the `else` branch immediately and comes back unchanged. It looks like it might get run through `camelKey` by mistake, since it's shaped like a key, but the function never treats a value as a key.

snippets.label: null is a value like any other, and its key still gets renamed
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
fun camelKey(s) = do {
  var parts = s splitBy "_"
  var rest = parts[1 to -1] default []
  ---
  parts[0] ++ ((rest map ((w) -> upper(w[0] default "") ++ (w[1 to -1] default ""))) joinBy "")
}
fun rewrite(v) = v match {
  case o is Object -> o mapObject ((val, key) -> { (camelKey(key)): rewrite(val) })
  case a is Array -> a map rewrite($)
  else -> v
}
---
rewrite(payload)
snippets.note: `first_name`'s key is renamed even though its value is `null` — the recursion doesn't skip a key just because there was nothing to walk into. And `account_status`'s value, `"in_progress"`, keeps its underscore: only the key beside it changed.
